1.why: All screens use a clean bold sans-serif with clear label/field spacing and comfortable line height, though the dark 'Logs' panel uses a small monospace font.

2.why: No italics or all-caps are used and every instruction is a single short sentence rather than a dense paragraph.

3.why: Content sits in a single narrow column with large full-width buttons and inputs that would read well on a phone, though the developer 'Logs' block adds non-essential content.

4.why: Copy such as 'Sign in first. Then we will help you add your authenticator.' and 'We can send one short code to your email or phone.' is short and plain.

5.why: Placeholders show expected input formats: 'name@example.com' for email and 'Example: 123456' for the verification code.

6.why: No screen requires reading more than one or two short sentences before acting.

7.why: No copy-to-clipboard control appears anywhere; the only code shown must be typed into the field, and the authenticator secret/recovery-code screens are never reached.

8.why: No QR code or equivalent alternative to manual entry is present in any screenshot; the flow stalls at 'Step 2 of 4' identity check.

9.why: Standard native email/password/text inputs are used which browsers may autofill, but there is no visible evidence of autocomplete or one-time-code support.

10.why: A 'Step 2 of 4 · Check identity' banner and a solid blue primary button are prominent, though the step indicator never advances and two blue buttons compete on later screens.

11.why: Step 3 onward presents three stacked actions at once — 'Send code', 'Check code' and 'Send a new code' — plus a delivery-method dropdown.

12.why: Green confirmations like 'Signed in. Next, check it is you.' and 'A code was sent. Enter the 6 numbers when you are ready.' state outcomes, but stale/duplicated banners ('A new code is ready' plus 'A code was sent') appear together.

13.why: 'Send a new code' allows unpenalised re-requests and retries, but there is no reveal/hide control and no secret or recovery codes are ever displayed.

14.why: The error reads 'That code did not match. Check the 6 numbers or send a new code.' — it names the problem and the fix without blaming the user.

15.why: No countdown, expiry timer, or auto-refreshing element is visible, and messages say 'when you are ready', though no explicit expiry policy is stated.
